method: Independent re-audit of ROADMAP-REVIEW.md v2 against PRD §§11/12/13/15/17, OPERATING-RULES §§7-8, phase-0/GO-NO-GO.md, phase-3/README.md exit criteria, phase-3.2 BUILD-NOTES/SPIKE, telemetry/runs.jsonl (12 rows), tools/orchestrate-review.py, tools/PHASE-0.5-CLOSE.md, phase-1 executor prompt + RUN-LEDGER, phase-2/3 KI-2, and v1 panel findings. No production code modified.
verdict_rationale: v2 corrected the material v1 errors (Phase 0.5 treated as unbuilt; orchestration treated as never-run; forgeable signing key listed open; §12 conflicting with PRD §13). The roadmap conclusion is now sound: stabilize orchestration just enough, run H-CI before evidence-tier extension, rewrite Act 2 as command-orchestrated, treat clean nulls as valid completion with named gaps. Remaining findings refine sequencing, fix residual factual nits, and tighten rules — they do not reverse the conclusion.

findings.claim: 12 telemetry rows in runs.jsonl, 8 from orchestrated runs with real decisions.
evidence: telemetry/runs.jsonl: wc -l => 12 rows, all phase-3.2
Rows 1-2 envelope_path = phase-3.2/reviews/review-{grok,gemini}-envelope.json (non-orchestrated path)
Rows 3-12 envelope_path = phase-3.2/reviews/orchestrated/* (10 rows, not 8)
Decisions present: ACCEPT×6, ACCEPT-WITH-NITS×2, REJECT×2, ERROR×1, UNKNOWN×1; non-zero token runs on successful rows
findings.recommended_change: Correct to 10 orchestrated rows + 2 prior manual/scripted review rows. Keep the partial-success + residual flakiness characterization (ERROR/UNKNOWN still real).
findings.risk_if_ignored: Small credibility nick on a document whose v1 failure mode was miscounting the system of record; easy to fix, easy to weaponize if left wrong.

findings.claim: Residual orchestration flakiness is empty/0-byte envelopes; Priority 1 harden list is adapter shim + fail on empty envelopes + multi-run determinism + keep telemetry append.
evidence: phase-3.2/reviews/orchestrated/review-grok-4.5-envelope.json currently 8120 bytes; gemini envelope 2961 bytes — not 0-byte
0-byte files currently observed: phase-3.2/reviews/roadmap-review-grok-envelope.json and roadmap-review-v2-gemini-envelope.json (roadmap-review artifacts, not the orchestrated product path)

phase-3.2/reviews/orchestrated/review-summary.json gate=STOP with stray_writes listing untracked review docs (ROADMAP-REVIEW.md, REVIEW-PROMPT.md, findings JSON) — dirty-tree false positive, not validator mutation of product code
tools/orchestrate-review.py step3_check_stray_writes: excludes only review_output_dir + orchestrate-review.py itself; no pre-run baseline snapshot of already-dirty paths
tools/orchestrate-review.py docstring cites tools/run-with-model.sh and tools/adapters/factory.py; body invokes DROID_BIN directly and raw-parses envelope['usage']['input_tokens'] at lines 160-161
findings.recommended_change: Retarget residual flakiness: (a) ERROR/UNKNOWN verdict rows and non-deterministic re-runs are the live defects; (b) add stray-write baseline/allowlist so a dirty worktree does not STOP a clean validator; (c) name dual missed reuse — adapter shim AND run-with-model.sh. Empty-envelope fail-closed remains good defense-in-depth but is not the currently observed primary failure mode on the orchestrated path.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Priority 1 'fixes' a stale symptom, leaves the false-positive STOP that breaks N-run H-CI, and under-specifies what 'stable enough for N identical runs' actually requires.

findings.claim: Priority 0 is reconstruction + valid-red closure first; then harden orchestration; then H-CI; then demo. Deadlock check claims no later priority is a hidden prerequisite.
evidence: Telemetry reconstruction is mechanical hygiene for §13 SoR; it does not unblock H-CI, Act 1 packaging, or Act 2
tools/PHASE-0.5-CLOSE.md already supplies Act 1 substance — packaging can start immediately and in parallel (review's own deadlock check admits this, but P0 does not schedule it)
phase-2/KNOWN-ISSUES.md KI-2 + phase-3/KNOWN-ISSUES.md KI-2: validator Execute write vector is detective-only; review §3.13 correctly calls this a demo blocker for 'read-only validators'
§4 P3 schedules demo packaging without requiring a preventive KI-2 fix; §4 P4 leaves KI-2-ish work in calibration backlog
PRD.md:531 v1 acceptance criterion still requires a controlled drill of retry/re-plan/human-decision — distinct from reopening Phase 2 completion under PRD §13 null-result rule
findings.recommended_change: Reshape near-term capacity to three parallelizable tracks, not a six-bucket serial program: (T1) cheap closures — run valid-red.py + 3–4 invalid-RED fixtures; package Act 1 from 0.5; optional telemetry reconstruct as non-gating hygiene. (T2) orchestration harden just enough for H-CI — adapter + run-with-model, empty-envelope fail-closed, stray-write baseline, deterministic multi-run — then H-CI N-run as the economic fork. (T3) demo honesty — rewrite Act 2 command-orchestrated; preventive KI-2 (read-only runner or throwaway checkout) before any 'read-only validator' / enforced-independence beat; drop or qualify 'close the laptop'. Keep PRD §12 controlled drill as an MVP acceptance item in the calibration track, labeled calibration/acceptance — not a Phase-2 reopen.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Serial P0 reconstruction burns attention without leverage; demo Act 2 ships with a known independence hole; MVP acceptance still fails the written controlled-drill criterion while the roadmap pretends foundations are settled.

findings.claim: Act 3 = Phase-0-verified controls only: model pinning, Droid Shield, OpenTelemetry traces.
evidence: phase-0/GO-NO-GO.md invariant scorecard and exit criteria verify model pinning (Probe 2), hook enforcement (Probe 4), isolation path (Probe 3), plugin scaffold (Probe 6) — not a PASS line for Droid Shield or OpenTelemetry export
PRD.md:636-644 Act 3 lists model rules, Droid Shield, deployment flexibility, OpenTelemetry — and itself says 'Build Act 3 only on capabilities Phase 0 verified'
ROADMAP-REVIEW §5 §16 correctly states the binding rule but §4 P3 re-lists Droid Shield and OTel as if already verified
findings.recommended_change: Act 3 demo beats = only controls with Phase-0 evidence (pinned models fail-closed, reference guard / locked-test hook, isolation guard, per-role invocation). List Droid Shield / OTel / air-gap as roadmap narrative only until re-probed. Apply §16 to the review's own Act 3 bullet list.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Demo Act 3 overclaims the same way Act 2 overclaimed Mission — the exact failure §16 was written to prevent.

findings.claim: A phase that completes without telemetry rows in the system of record has not met its exit criteria, even if the envelope JSONs exist on disk.
evidence: ROADMAP-REVIEW §3.2 correctly argues §13 inputs are partially recoverable from committed envelopes + gen-telemetry.py
tools/PHASE-0.5-CLOSE.md used tools/RUN-LEDGER.md as the cost/intervention SoR, not telemetry/runs.jsonl
phase-1/RUN-LEDGER.md is structured cost data outside runs.jsonl
§10 as written would retroactively void Phase 0.5/1/2 completions that have envelopes/ledgers but no runs.jsonl rows
findings.recommended_change: Rewrite §10 forward-looking: from adoption forward, multi-invocation phases must emit runs.jsonl (and findings/dispositions when applicable) from the orchestration script. Committed envelopes + auditable reconstruction recipes remain valid evidence for past phases and for disaster recovery. Do not equate 'missing live SoR row' with 'phase incomplete' when reconstructable artifacts exist.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Rule creates paper incompleteness, contradicts the reconstruction plan in §3.2/§4 P0, and incentivizes busywork over measurement.

findings.claim: If the script doesn't exist yet, the first deliverable of the phase is to build it; capacity envelope refuses unbounded foundation programs.
evidence: §9 spike exception is sound; 'first deliverable is the script' for every multi-invocation phase can re-expand Priority 1 into a foundation program
§4 still lists Priority 0–5 (six buckets) while §17 and the capacity stanza say name 1–3 deliverables
phase-0/GO-NO-GO.md Phase 1 build order wanted a thin per-role wrapper, not today's full multi-validator orchestrate-review.py
findings.recommended_change: Tighten §9: script the invocations the phase will actually repeat; do not require a full panel orchestrator as Phase-N's first deliverable unless the phase exit needs N-run review. Reconcile §17 with §4 by naming the actual next 1–3 deliverables in the capacity stanza (e.g. valid-red closure, orchestration harden-for-H-CI, H-CI N-run) and marking the rest as ordered backlog, not active priorities.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Capacity rule is theater while the priority list remains an unbounded program; thin vertical slices get blocked on orchestration completeness.

findings.claim: With a stabilized orchestrator, run the full N-run A/B; H-CI is the economic fork that decides further evidence-tier investment.
evidence: phase-3.2/SPIKE.md §3: only evidence source changes; fairness rule counts bundle-read tokens; null result redirects to panel-size/context levers
phase-3.2/BUILD-NOTES.md + chunk1-token-accounting.json: directional 55.2% saving on full-suite combined raw, fairness does not hold at locked-test-only scope — review states this correctly
H-CI primary metric is tokens-to-same-ACCEPT at equal quality; it needs a stable evidence produce+consume path and comparable validator runs, not every future orchestration feature
findings.recommended_change: Keep H-CI before Harness/3.3/dogfood (uncontested). Explicitly bound P1 to the minimum needed for credible N-run A/B (deterministic invoke, parseable envelopes, correct token fields via adapter, worktree isolation). Do not gate H-CI on demo packaging, telemetry reconstruction, or full KI-2 preventive redesign.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Either H-CI slips behind unrelated demo polish, or P1 expands until the economic fork never runs.

findings.claim: v2 missed-win set (§3.1–3.14) is the material set after panel additions.
evidence: Accurate and still material: §3.4 invalid-RED, §3.5 review-tests (take the L), §3.6 Phase 3 exits, §3.7 executor given the answer, §3.10 adapter bypass, §3.11–3.14 panel additions
§3.8 correctly closed; residual key-distribution note is right
§3.9 Gemini non-blocking-not-no-op is right; 3.2 orchestrated REJECT/ACCEPT pairs strengthen it

Additional missed win under-weighted: orchestrate-review.py also bypasses tools/run-with-model.sh (docstring-cited enforcement wrapper) — family/model pinning discipline is not only an adapter concern
Additional process gap: review-summary gate STOP on dirty worktree means 'scripted' runs are still not hermetic — belongs next to §3.1/§3.10
findings.recommended_change: Add a short §3.x (or fold into §3.10): orchestration bypasses both the adapter shim and run-with-model.sh; stray-write check is not hermetic against pre-existing dirty trees. No need to expand the missed-win list further.
findings.risk_if_ignored: P1 harden checklist stays incomplete; N-run stability work misses the actual STOP failure mode.

findings.claim: Unexercised safety paths are named gaps/calibration, not phase blockers; mine existing disagreement before manufacturing new ones.
evidence: PRD.md:572: clean null is valid; manufactured disagreement is not a success gate — v2 §12 rewrite is correct
PRD.md:531 v1 acceptance still wants one controlled drill of rejection→retry/re-plan/human-decision
Existing corpora: Phase 2 amendments path, Phase 3.1 panel split, Phase 3.2 orchestrated grok REJECT vs gemini ACCEPT — review lists these correctly
findings.recommended_change: Keep §12 as rewritten. In P4, add an explicit MVP-acceptance line: one controlled rejection drill before v1 acceptance claims, fed preferably by replaying an existing REJECT corpus through the retry state machine rather than inventing new blocking findings. Label it acceptance/calibration, not phase-completion.
findings.risk_if_ignored: Either the controlled drill stays forever-deferred while claiming MVP, or someone reopens honest null phases — both worse than naming it once in P4.

findings.claim: Current roadmap order is Harness → H-CI → 3.3 → dogfood; this is backwards; evidence-tier extension only if H-CI non-null.
evidence: phase-3.2/BUILD-NOTES.md follow-ons list Harness before full H-CI — review's read is fair
phase-3.2/SPIKE.md §3.5: null result is valid and redirects levers — review correctly preserves this
Agree without contest: do not build Harness/3.3/dogfood as the next active investment before H-CI
findings.recommended_change: No change to the deferral. Optional clarification only: a null H-CI may still justify a thin flavor-(a) CI-as-runner for coverage/reliability, but not flavor-(b) Harness-native investment as a cost play.

missed_wins_scorecard.note: Late/flaky orchestration is real; row split is 10 orchestrated not 8; primary residual is ERROR/UNKNOWN + dirty-tree STOP, not currently-empty orchestrated envelopes.
SoR incomplete but recoverable — correct framing.
True calibration gap; v2 correctly avoids manufactured-disagreement gates. Still need one MVP controlled drill somewhere.
Cheap to close; belongs in near-term track.
Take the L is the right disposition.
Fix verified in local_backend.py/consumer.py; residual is key distribution.
Non-blocking not no-op; 3.2 splits add evidence.

adjustments: Do not serialize telemetry reconstruction ahead of H-CI/demo-honesty work; make it non-gating hygiene.
Parallel Track A (cheap closures): valid-red.py + invalid-RED fixtures; Act 1 packaging from PHASE-0.5-CLOSE; optional telemetry reconstruct.

Serial Track B (economic fork): minimal orchestration harden (adapter, run-with-model, empty-envelope fail-closed, stray-write baseline, deterministic multi-run) → H-CI N-run with provider tokenizers.

Serial Track C (demo honesty, can overlap B after harden): rewrite Act 2 command-orchestrated; preventive KI-2 before read-only-validator claims; Act 3 only on Phase-0-evidenced controls; no close-laptop claim without a durable runner.
Backlog D (calibration/MVP acceptance, not gates for B): mine disagreement corpora; one controlled rejection drill for PRD §12; Gemini precision; review-tests remains taken L.
Backlog E (only after H-CI): Harness flavor-(b) / 3.3 / dogfood if non-null or explicitly accepted as coverage-not-cost.
proposed_resequence.why_not_reject: v2 already adopted the load-bearing corrections from v1 REJECT (0.5 exists, orchestration partially runs, §12 null-result safe, H-CI before Harness, Act 2 rewrite, capacity envelope). Remaining issues change ordering detail and rule sharpness, not the roadmap thesis.

accept_with_edits: §9 — keep spike exception; bound 'first deliverable' to the phase's actual repeat surface, not a full panel orchestrator by default
§10 — forward-looking script emission required; do not void past phases with reconstructable envelopes/ledgers
§12 — keep v2 rewrite; add MVP controlled-drill pointer in calibration backlog
§14 — extend to run-with-model.sh / any cited enforcement wrapper, not only adapters/factory.py
§17 — force the capacity stanza to name 1–3 active deliverables; everything else is ordered backlog
add: Hermetic stray-write checks: baseline the tree before validator invoke; only new paths outside the allowlist count as KI-2 violations
Optional but useful: when a docstring cites a shim/wrapper, the implementation must call it or the citation is a §8-style silent scope lie
